verdict.rationale: Docusaurus is a local, file-based static site generator. You scaffold a project with create-docusaurus, write MDX files, and build static output, so docs can live in your own repository. Its docs name git as a translation workflow, list deployment targets such as GitHub Pages, Vercel and Netlify, and a community user describes migrating their 'docs-as-code' to it. However, the evidence never documents branch, pull-request or merge-driven publishing as a Docusaurus feature; that behavior would come from the hosting or CI platform. missing for 10: documented git-branch/PR/merge-triggered publish workflow, PR preview deployments, first-party git integration docs.

support.subject: As a developer, my docs live in my own git repository — branches, pull requests, and merges drive what gets published

citations.quote: Simply write docs and blog posts with MDX, and Docusaurus builds them into static HTML files ready to be served.
Use git, Crowdin, or any other translation manager to translate your docs and deploy them individually.
You can deploy your site to static site hosting services such as [Vercel](https://vercel.com/), [GitHub Pages](https://pages.github.com/), [Netlify](https://www.netlify.com/)
I tried migrating our markdown docs-as-code to use Docusaurus
